title: Two unit orientations of the same plane both take absolute value 1 on a common covector
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P, and let ξ_1, ξ_2 ∈ MultiVector P n both be unit orientations of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_k Q for k = 1, 2: there are orthonormal families τ, τ' spanning Q and signs with ξ_1(α) = ±α(τ) and ξ_2(α) = ±α(τ') for every n-covector α). Then there is an n-covector α on ℝ^P (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n) with |ξ_1(α)| = 1 and |ξ_2(α)| = 1. (With ξ_1 = ξ_2 this shows that a unit orientation is non-zero.)
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ₁ ξ₂ : MultiVector P n), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ₁ Q → IsUnitOrientationOf ξ₂ Q → ∃ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ₁ α| = 1 ∧ |ξ₂ α| = 1
